item.title: Short AI Use Reduces Focus and Persistence, New Study Shows
item.description:
Short AI Use Reduces Focus and Persistence, New Study Shows

A peer‑reviewed study presented this week at the Conference on Language Modeling found that just ten minutes of AI assistance can significantly impair people’s ability to stay focused and persist on difficult tasks.

🔍 Overview

  • The research was led by a multinational team that includes scholars from Carnegie Mellon University, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, the University of Oxford, UCLA, and a research fellow with the UC Berkeley Center for Human‑Compatible AI, Brian Christian.
  • The paper builds on earlier preliminary drafts that generated media coverage from WIRED, Psychology Today, and the New York Times.

⚙️ Study Design

  • Researchers ran three randomized controlled trials with a total of 1,222 online participants.
  • Experiment 1 (354 participants): one group solved 15 basic fraction problems alone, another group solved the same problems with ChatGPT open for assistance and answer requests.
  • Experiment 2 (667 participants): a larger replication of the fraction‑problem design.
  • Experiment 3 (201 participants): participants tackled an SAT‑style reading‑comprehension prompt under the same AI‑access vs. no‑AI conditions.

📊 Key Findings

  • In the first experiment, the AI‑access group started off more accurate than the no‑AI group.
  • After participants completed 12 problems, the AI tool was removed.
  • Immediate drop: the AI‑access group’s accuracy and persistence fell sharply as soon as ChatGPT was taken away.
  • In the larger second experiment, AI users either gave wrong answers or gave up entirely when assistance was withdrawn, while the no‑AI group continued working and ended with higher success.
  • The third experiment echoed the same pattern: removal of the AI tool led to reduced persistence and accuracy on the reading task.
  • The authors conclude that short‑term reliance on AI erodes “cognitive fitness” by eliminating the “productive struggle” that helps people develop research strengths and passions.

💡 Why It Matters

  • Overreliance on AI for rapid answers can make slower, effortful problem‑solving feel inefficient.
  • Frontier AI companies acknowledge that offloading tasks to chatbots can lower baseline understanding and mastery of subjects.
  • Christian warns that in research and academia, excessive AI assistance could jeopardize core scientific habits: staying close to data, immersing in material, and collaborating in teams.
  • He suggests AI responses could default to a more instructive, tutor‑like style rather than providing instant answers.

🧑‍🤝‍🧑 Team Affiliations

Institution Role
Carnegie Mellon University Scholar
Massachusetts Institute of Technology Scholar
University of Oxford Scholar
UCLA Scholar
UC Berkeley Center for Human‑Compatible AI Research Fellow (Brian Christian)

Images below illustrate the experimental results and the research team.

#AI #CognitiveScience #HumanComputerInteraction #Education

Source: Just 10 Minutes of AI Use May Erode Persistence on Hard Tasks

item.title: Free Vibe Coding Workshop Series Teaches AI-Driven Software Creation
item.description:
Free Vibe Coding Workshop Series Teaches AI-Driven Software Creation

WIT // HSV and ARC are hosting a free, three‑part Vibe Coding Workshop Series that shows participants how to turn natural‑language prompts into working software using AI‑powered code generators.

🔍 Overview

  • Hands‑on, immersive workshops (not lectures) that guide AI tools to generate, iterate, and improve code.
  • Series consists of three 2‑hour modules for a total of 6 hours of instruction.
  • Open to professionals, students, educators, creators, and curious minds.

🧩 How it works

  • Vibe coding lets you build functional software simply by describing intent in natural language.
  • Participants will explore cloud‑native AI app builders to turn ideas into interactive applications without writing code manually.
Platform Role
Lovable Cloud‑native AI app builder
Bolt.new Cloud‑native AI app builder
Google AI Studio Cloud‑native AI app builder

⚙️ Key Details

  • Free to attend – no cost for participants.
  • Open to all – no prerequisites or prior coding experience required.

  • Workshop schedule:

🚀 Availability

  • Register now to secure a spot; the event is free and open to everyone.
  • 👉 For more information on the three‑part workshop series, click here.

  • The barrier between having an idea and building something that works is disappearing.

item.title: University of Notre Dame Hosts AI Coding Assistant Security Workshop
item.description:
University of Notre Dame Hosts AI Coding Assistant Security Workshop

On Thursday, October 8, 2026, the AI Collaborative Programming group offered a virtual, hands‑on workshop where participants put AI coding assistants to the test in a web‑application security sandbox.

🔍 Overview

  • Date & Time: Thursday, October 8, 2026, 1:00 pm – 2:00 pm
  • Format: Virtual (250I Hesburgh Library link)
  • Goal: Identify and patch common security flaws using AI‑assisted tools while maintaining strict human oversight.

🛠️ Workshop Content

  • Work with AI tools such as GitHub Copilot or VS Code alongside an OWASP Juice Shop instance.
  • Follow a human‑in‑the‑loop workflow:
    • Isolate a vulnerability.
    • Create a Git branch.
    • Prompt the AI for a secure fix.
    • Verify the patch against insecure defaults.
    • Write clean PR documentation.
  • Learn to:
    • Critique AI‑generated code.
    • Spot dangerous hallucinations.
    • Maintain rigorous developer oversight.

👥 Presenters & Audience

Name Role
Rob Wieck Senior Research Software Engineer / Product Owner, AI Enablement
Julie Vecchio Interim Co‑Director, Navari Family Center for Digital Scholarship
  • Open to: Undergraduate and graduate students, faculty, staff, and postdocs.

📅 Details

  • Part of a series offered by the AI Collaborative Programming group, a partnership between Hesburgh Libraries, ND Learning, and the Office of Information Technology.
  • Location for the virtual session: 250I Hesburgh Library.

💡 Why It Matters

  • Demonstrates practical ways to integrate AI coding assistants into secure software development.
  • Emphasizes the importance of human review to mitigate AI‑generated errors.
  • Provides a reproducible sandbox for learning secure coding practices.

#AI #CodingAssistants #WebSecurity #Workshop

Source: AI Masterclass: Developer Hands-On With AI-Assisted Coding Tools and OWASP Juice Shop

item.title: a16z Launches Horowitz Andreessen Academy for Silicon Valley Startup Pipeline
item.description:
a16z Launches Horowitz Andreessen Academy for Silicon Valley Startup Pipeline

Venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) is creating the Horowitz Andreessen Academy, a pipeline designed for young people to build or join a Silicon Valley startup.

🔍 Overview

Led by a16z with $42 million in funding, the academy is described as a “highly selective school” that does not grant any accreditation or degree. It is designed mainly for recent high school graduates.

🧩 How it works

The program replaces traditional academic structures with a focus on industry experience:

  • Curriculum: Short, high-impact classes led by tech figureheads, such as OpenAI CEO Sam Altman.
  • Practical Experience: “Co-ops” that provide students with roles at tech companies.
  • Assessment: There are no traditional grades, tests, or homework.

⚙️ Key details

Students in the program are provided with specific financial and technical resources:

  • More than $50,000 in compute credits
  • A $5,000 travel and research budget offered by a16z
Partner Role
Anduril Partner
Anthropic Partner
Coinbase Partner
Google Partner
Meta Partner
Nvidia Partner
OpenAI Partner
Palantir Partner
Replit Partner
Stripe Partner

🚀 Availability

  • Launch Date: The first one-year program begins in the fall of 2027.
  • Cost: The first program will be free.
  • Capacity: Only 50 students will be accepted.
  • Requirements: Students must move to San Francisco and arrange their own housing.

💡 Why it matters

The academy follows a trend of Silicon Valley billionaires, including Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, and Jeff Bezos, investing in their own schools. a16z founders Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz have been critical of colleges; Andreessen reportedly called the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and Stanford “political lobbying operations fighting American innovation” in a group chat with tech leaders and White House officials.

#a16z #SiliconValley #Education #Startups

Source: Andreessen Horowitz is launching an ‘academy’ with no homework and partnerships with Palantir, Google, and Meta

item.title: New Educational Programs for Agentic AI and AI Engineering
item.description:
New Educational Programs for Agentic AI and AI Engineering

Several new educational programs have been introduced to teach agentic AI, focusing on systems that can perform tasks, use tools, make decisions, and complete multi-step workflows with limited human intervention.

🔍 Overview

Agentic AI differs from basic chatbots through its ability to utilize tools and manage complex workflows. Key technical concepts include:

  • Agentic RAG: Combines retrieval capabilities with agent-based decision-making.
  • Multi-agent systems: Allows multiple specialized agents to work together.

⚙️ Key details

Comprehensive curricula for agentic AI are designed to go beyond basic prompt engineering, covering the following technical areas:

  • Architecture and Frameworks: AI agent architecture, LangGraph, and CrewAI for multi-agent workflows.
  • Development: LLM APIs, function calling, structured outputs, tool use, and API/system integrations.
  • Data and Memory: Vector databases, memory, and retrieval.
  • Operations: Agent evaluation, monitoring, observability, error handling, fallback strategies, and production deployment.

Practical workflows taught in these courses include automating repetitive tasks, connecting AI tools, creating business workflows, using AI for research and analysis, and designing practical AI use cases.

🚀 Availability

Program Focus and Key Features
IITM Pravartak Practical skills in AI agents, agentic workflows, AI engineering, RAG, and deployable agent systems.
IIT Roorkee (via Futurense) Combines generative AI fundamentals with agentic AI concepts.
PG Certificate in Building Professional Agentic AI with AIOps Combines agentic AI development with AIOps.
PG Certificate in AI-Driven LLM, SLM, Agentic RAG Development Focuses on language models (large and small) and retrieval-based AI systems.
Residential PG Diploma in AI/ML and Agentic AI Engineering Combines AI and machine learning foundations with agentic AI engineering.

#AgenticAI #AIEducation #LLM #AIOps #RAG

Source: Best Agentic AI Courses in India 2026 | Futurense

item.title: LogicMojo AI Certification Course Rated Deep Across Full Stack for 2026 Hiring
item.description:
LogicMojo AI Certification Course Rated Deep Across Full Stack for 2026 Hiring

LogicMojo published a ranking of AI certification courses for 2026, highlighting one programme that scores Deep on every layer of its six‑layer stack.

🔍 Overview

  • Hundreds of programmes now sit between ₹0 and ₹4L+ with near‑identical landing pages, hiring logos and “industry‑recognised certificate” claims.
  • A certification is described as a receipt, not a result.
  • The ranking is disclosed as published by LogicMojo, which is ranked #1.
  • Five expert reviewers (Suvom Shaw, Rishabh Gupta, Sankalp Jain, Monesh Venkul Vommi, Mohamed Shirhaan) fact‑checked the analysis.
  • Ten courses were scored on a single question: “If I start now with a job, a laptop and 8–12 hours a week, how quickly does this make me genuinely hireable?”

⚙️ Scoring Methodology

  • Six open pillars form the scoring framework.
  • Coverage is a weighted share of the 17 Table 2 skill areas (Deep 4 · Good 3 · Moderate 2 · Basic 1).
  • Reach is an indicative brand‑recognition index (author estimate, not enrolment data).
  • Seven tables and ten reviews support the scores.
  • Every section names where other options beat the evaluated programme.

📚 Curriculum Depth

  • Foundations start from Python and data handling; maths is taught as intuition tied to model behaviour.
  • Core ML covers ensembles, metric selection, imbalanced data and error analysis.
  • Deep learning includes real training runs, not just architecture diagrams.
  • The programme is the only one rated Deep on all six layers, including the three commonly skipped layers: production RAG, fine‑tuning and agents.

🚀 Delivery & Career Support

  • Live teaching delivered in Indian time zones.
  • Every project is peer‑reviewed and portfolio‑ready.
  • Support includes mentorship, resume preparation, mock interviews, job referrals and placement assistance.
  • The author could not verify any placement rate and therefore makes no claim about it.

💰 Value & Pricing

  • Depth comparable to programmes normally priced above ₹2L+ is offered at a mid‑band price.
  • No parallel catalogue of marketing, finance or product courses competes for curriculum attention; the syllabus is kept current.

💡 Why it matters

  • Provides a faster path to a job‑ready AI profile aligned with 2026 hiring needs.
  • Helps differentiate genuine depth from superficial certificates that merely act as receipts.
  • Enables learners to assess options side‑by‑side based on live teaching, curriculum quality, practical projects and career support.

#AICertification #JobReadyAI #AIEducation

Source: Top 10 Best AI Certification Courses to Become Job Ready Faster (2026)

item.title: OECD Study Finds Students Using AI Perform Worse Without Critical Assessment Training
item.description:
OECD Study Finds Students Using AI Perform Worse Without Critical Assessment Training

According to newly released data from the OECD’s Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA), students who use artificial intelligence to help them study tend to perform worse at school than those who do not. The study, which collected data in 2025, represents the first time PISA has evaluated student performance since AI tools went truly mainstream.

📊 Scope of the study

The PISA study evaluated 15-year-old students across science, math, and reading. Key findings regarding student demographics and global trends include:

  • Global scale: The data draws from over 760,000 students across 91 countries.
  • Socioeconomic factors: After adjusting for socioeconomic status, students who never use AI generally outperformed those who do in science. AI use was found to be more common among students from relatively advantaged backgrounds, which likely reflects better access to hardware, stable internet access, and paid AI tools.
  • Geographic variation: AI utilization varies widely by country. For example, over 95 percent of Vietnamese students reported using AI tools, compared to just 60 percent in Japan.
  • Curiosity connection: The study noted that student curiosity levels correlate with AI use, peaking among daily users.

⚙️ Performance by AI task and frequency

The relationship between AI use and academic performance is complex, with results heavily dependent on how and how often the tools are used.

Method of AI Use Performance Impact
Summarizing texts or drafting writing assignments Relatively worse performance
Preliminary research or broad “help me learn” use Less of a performance drop
Weekly use to generally help learn Outperformed non-users (though not by much)
Weekly general help + critical assessment training All regular users outperformed non-users

Frequency of use also plays a significant role in student outcomes:

  • Daily or yearly use: Students who used AI daily, as well as those who only used it once or twice a year, tended to perform the worst.
  • Weekly or monthly use: Better academic results were seen among monthly or weekly AI users.

💡 Intentional learning vs. shortcutting

The study’s authors suggest that “moderate and intentional use of AI for schoolwork and learning” could have positive effects, especially when students are trained to critically assess the information they receive.

OECD director of learning and skills Andreas Schleicher explained the cognitive dynamics of using technology in education:

“In the same way that we do not become fit by watching sports but by doing sports, learning does not occur through the consumption of content, but as a productive cognitive struggle of the mind with new material,” Schleicher wrote. “Where technology enables or enhances that cognitive struggle, students will advance.”

Conversely, Schleicher added: “Where technology short-circuits the productive struggle of learning, it will undercut students’ development.”

#PISA #OECD #EdTech #AIinEducation

Source: Students who use AI generally score worse at school
